newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzuki aims to boost compact car sales.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki aims to boost compact car sales.

text.p: Suzuki Motor Corp plans to strengthen its sales of new compact cars in Japan until new minivehicles are launched in or after October 1998, Suzuki president Osamu Suzuki told reporters.
"We will launch new compact models to boost sales until we launch new minivehicles meeting the new standard," he said.
Last October, the Transport Ministry said Japan's classification of minivehicles would change in October 1998 to enhance safety in collisions.

Under the new rules, to be classified as a mini, a vehicle can be no longer than 3.4 metres or wider than 1.48 metres with an engine displacement of 660 cc. This compares with the current 1990 standard of a maximum length of 3.3 metres and a maximum width of 1.4 metres, with same engine size.

"We have six minivehicles in our lineup now. We cannot introduce those six models in a new body size at the same time. We will launch new minivehicles meeting the new standard gradually by October 1998," Suzuki said.

Suzuki earlier forecast it would achieve domestic sales of 635,000 vehicles in 1997, up 2.0 percent from 1996. Projected 1997 domestic sales included 75,000 compact cars, up 13 percent from a year earlier after an 8.0 percent gain in 1996.
